## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile/tablet-friendly 3D game combining Pokémon-like companionship with Elden Ring-style action combat.

## Requirements
- Create the game now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Support phones and tablets with responsive layout and usable touch controls.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created an original fantasy action game, “Emberwild,” with a companion fox and a telegraphed boss fight rather than using copyrighted Pokémon characters.
- Used Three.js from a CDN and authored the 3D scene from procedural geometry.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a 3D forest arena, player character, ember-fox companion, Cindermaw boss, combat, dodge, healing flask, HUD, keyboard/mouse inputs, and touch joystick/action buttons.
- Added responsive visual styling and start/victory/defeat screens.
- Started a local server and captured/inspected `screenshots/current.jpg`; screenshot showed the game render after fixing an initialization-order bug.

### Active
- Verify gameplay interactions and refine any issues found in the screenshot or browser checks.
- Review `git status` and summarize the completed implementation for the user.

### Blocked
- Browser console reports a favicon 404 (`http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico`); non-blocking.
- No further gameplay testing has been recorded.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest `screenshots/current.jpg` if visual refinement is needed, and test controls/combat in the browser.
2. Check for JavaScript errors during gameplay and fix any issues.
3. Report the game features, controls, assumptions, and validation status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and HUD markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive desktop/mobile layout and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, gameplay mechanics, inputs, and combat.
- `screenshots/current.jpg`: Latest browser screenshot.

## Important Context
- Local server was launched with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- `game.js` initially had a `ReferenceError: renderer is not defined` because scene setup was absent; the renderer and world setup were subsequently added.
- Browser console after that fix showed only the favicon 404 and WebGL readback performance warnings.
